newsitem.title: USA: D&P puts Figgie Int'l on watch-uncertain.
newsitem.headline: D&P puts Figgie Int'l on watch-uncertain.

text.p: Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co said Monday it has placed the rating of Figgie International Inc.'s senior notes on rating watch - uncertain.
The $174 million 9.875 percent senior notes are currently rated double-B-minus.

D&P said the rating action follows Figgie's announcement that it has entered into a definitive agreement to sell its Snorkel division, a manufacturer of aerial work platforms, for $150 million in cash, plus assumed liabilities.

Snorkel has been a key component of Figgie's operations and profitability, providing 41 percent of sales and operating profit in 1996. While the sale greatly enhances Figgie's financial flexibility (pro forma cash of $195 million exceeds the company's $186 million debt level at March 31, 1997), the company has indicated that it plans to use the sale proceeds to launch an aggressive growth strategy, particularly focused on strategic acquisitions for its Scott Aviation division.
The rating review will focus on the expected returns from the re-deployed sale proceeds, the resulting capital structure and incoming management's long-term strategic plans, D&P said.

The company, which expects to name a new chief executive officer in late August, has been seeking a permanent CEO since its former top executive, who has remained chairman of the board, resigned in January.
Also, as a part of the rating review, D&P said it will monitor developments with respect to the $276 million unsolicited offer for Figgie made by Heico Holding, a private investment firm, on July 3.

Following the Snorkel divestiture, Figgie will be a less diversified and more focused entity with core businesses that include Scott Aviation, a manufacturer of protective breathing and oxygen equipment, and Interstate Electronics, a manufacturer of sophisticated electronic systems.
